lessons.title: New marks from texture
lessons.goal: I can try a rubbing to show a feeling.
success: I can try the new way with help if I need it.
I can choose one and say or show why.
words: How a surface feels or looks.
Move a tool back and forth.
With a small amount of force.
A small try before a piece.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: You can point, speak, sign or watch first.
Pick a made-up feeling for your art.
Today we will try texture rubbing.
stages.say: Show a safe piece of ridged card and a smooth card. We will put paper on top and rub a crayon across it. The bumps can make marks show through. This is a new way of making marks for our lessons. You may watch, direct me or use the silent option.
stages.good: Pupil chooses an invented feeling or confirms one. No personal story is needed.
stages.fallback: Offer two silent hand textures: a smooth glide or small uneven stops. Pupil can direct the adult.
stages.answer: Any chosen feeling is valid. A texture has no fixed emotional meaning.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Look at a smooth surface and one with ridges.
Which has bumps?
You may look without touching.
stages.say: Show the two surfaces. Ask permission before offering touch; do not place a pupil hand on an object. Describe flat and ridged. Ask how a rough-looking mark might suggest an invented feeling.
stages.good: Pupil notices an actual surface feature before suggesting a feeling.
stages.fallback: Adult makes a smooth hand path and a path with small stops; pupil identifies the difference.
stages.answer: Ridges are raised lines. Either texture can express calm or energy if the maker gives a reason.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Put safe card on the table.
Lay thin paper on top. Hold its edge.
Use the side of a crayon. Rub lightly.
Lift the paper. Look at the marks.
stages.say: 1. Put a clean, dry, flat piece of ridged card on a clear table. 2. Lay a small sheet of thin paper on it. Hold the paper at the edge, outside the rubbing area. 3. Lay a broad wax crayon on its side. Move it gently back and forth for four short sweeps. 4. Lift the paper and show the pattern. Make a second test on smoother card with the same crayon. If little shows, check paper contact, use thinner paper or try a little more pressure. Stop before paper tears. Heavy pressure can hide the pattern. Keep the two real tests.
stages.good: Adult demonstrates each step slowly and compares the actual prints, even if one is faint. This is rubbing over a surface, different from drawing each line or moving loose shapes.
stages.fallback: Model a new texture translation: one continuous hand glide, then four small stop-start moves. Hold each end pose for a slow count of two. Pupil chooses the movement texture. Call this silent movement, not a completed rubbing.
stages.answer: CfU: Is the textured card above or below the paper? Below. If unsure, lift the paper and reset it together, then ask again.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Help the adult make two tests.
Which marks can you see?
Choose a test for a made-up feeling.
Say: I chose ___ because ___.
stages.say: Pupils direct where the paper and crayon go. Compare the ridged and smoother tests. Ask each pupil for one choice. Hinge: the paper is tearing. A: press harder; B: stop and try lighter pressure. Show hands or point.
stages.good: Each pupil makes a choice and identifies a feature. They choose B for the tearing paper.
stages.fallback: Compare the smooth glide and stop-start motion. Pupil directs a lighter or smaller version if the movement is uncomfortable.
stages.answer: B. If A is chosen, show a gentle sweep on fresh scrap. Parallel check: to protect the next sheet, press hard or lightly? Lightly. Proceed when the pupil can choose a gentle action or direct one.

stages.name: Create
pupil: In your book or arts log, choose a feeling.
Make two small texture tests.
Pick the test that fits your idea.
Keep both tests and your own reason.
stages.say: Give each pupil two small sheets and two safe flat surfaces, or let them take turns at a stable shared tray. Repeat the four rubbing steps. Keep the colour the same while testing textures so the texture difference is clearer. The pupil chooses the preferred test. Adult help may hold paper or move the crayon under the pupil direction. Do not rub on skin, walls, fittings or sharp objects. Use familiar materials and the setting procedures.
stages.good: Two actual tests with a pupil-selected texture and a reason, or two witnessed silent movement textures with the same choice and reason. Completion does not require a tidy or dark rubbing.
stages.fallback: Make a smooth glide and a stop-start hand path, with a still end pose. Choose one texture for the invented feeling. Pupil may direct the adult or use eye-pointing. Staff record the actual movement method, not rubbing.
stages.answer: Example only: I chose ridges because the broken marks feel busy to me. A different reading is valid. Record what was actually tried.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Show the two tests to an adult.
Point to the texture you chose.
Say what you notice.
Tidy and keep the tests for next time.
stages.say: Share privately if preferred. Ask the pupil what the texture suggests to them. The listener says I notice, then checks the maker meaning. In the last two minutes collect crayons, stack clean card, collect scraps and keep tests in each pupil tray.
stages.good: The choice stays with the pupil; both tests are stored and no private feeling is inferred.
stages.fallback: Pupil repeats or directs the two motions. Adult notes their sequence and chosen version for tomorrow.
stages.answer: A useful observation names repeated ridges, faint patches or smooth movement rather than judging the maker.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: I tried ___.
My two tests were ___.
I chose ___ because ___.
Next time I will ___.
stages.say: Date the real work. Scribe the pupil own words if requested, then read them back. Note the actual help and method. Keep the tests for the next lesson. If only a rehearsal happened, record rehearsal honestly.
stages.good: Dated entry retains technique, two trials, choice, reason and support actually used.
stages.fallback: Pupil gives or confirms an oral log. Staff record it at the next opportunity with the true activity date.
stages.answer: Example only: I tried texture rubbing. I chose the ridged test because it feels full of energy.

Supported: Pick a feeling or point to a choice.
Direct an adult through two small tests.
Say or show why you chose it.
Independent: Make two texture tests with the same crayon.
Pick the texture that fits your idea.
Keep both tests and your reason.
Aspire: Try a lighter sweep on a small spare area.
Say what changes in the marks.
Choose a version for a reason.

log: The new way I tried was ___.
misconceptions: Pressing harder always gives a better rubbing
Use gentle pressure first. Too much force can tear the paper or hide texture.
Every pupil must touch a rough surface
Looking, directing an adult or using a silent movement texture is valid.
The same texture means the same feeling to everyone
Ask the maker for their meaning and reason.
kit: For four pupils: four books or arts logs, eight small sheets of thin paper, four broad wax crayons and four clear table spaces.
Provide four clean pieces of ridged card and four smooth pieces of card, with safe edges. Shared trays can be used in pairs. No cutting tools, wet paint or adhesive are needed.
Prepare two small real rubbings for demonstration, four storage trays and spare paper. Check that the surfaces give a visible mark before teaching.
No-materials route: seated or standing silent hand movement. No device, body contact or personal story is required.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Put ridged card on the table. Lay thin paper over it. Hold the paper edge.
15 to 30 seconds
Place the crayon on its side. Make four light back-and-forth sweeps.
30 to 45 seconds
Lift the paper. Notice the ridges. Make a small second test over smooth card.
45 to 60 seconds
Compare the actual marks. Choose a test and explain a possible feeling.
models: Teacher example only: the ridged marks suggest energy to me. Another maker may read them as calm.
Teacher example only: I used a smooth glide and stop-start hand movement. I chose the stops for surprise. This is movement evidence, not a rubbing.
comparison: Ridged card
Paper rests on ridges. Gentle rubbing can reveal repeated lines.
The broken lines might suggest energy.
Smoother card
Paper rests on a flatter surface. The rubbing may be more even.
The softer patch might suggest calm.

hinge.question: The paper starts to tear. What should the maker do?
hinge.feedback: B. Stop. Use fresh paper and a gentle sweep.
hinge.wrong_feedback: Stop before the paper tears more. Try a gentle sweep on fresh paper.

lessons.artist_use_note: Original classroom models only. No artwork, quotation or lyrics are reproduced. Model statements are not pupil evidence.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Give one step at a time, point to the current instruction and model the first step only. Keep the plan or test visible. Check understanding by asking the pupil to show the next step.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Allow pointing, sign, speech, gesture or an adult scribe. Give processing time. Read scribed words back for confirmation. Use I chose ... because ... .
adaptations.semh: Use invented or abstract ideas. Offer a quiet pause, private audience and a clear return cue. No personal disclosure, forced touch or public performance.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Offer seated silent movement, larger comfortable actions or pupil-directed adult making. Allow looking without touch. Keep sounds below talking volume.
adaptations.eal: Plan in any language. Model the key words with objects or gestures; accept a drawing or oral sequence before fuller sentences.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Artists and designers test a method, follow and adapt a plan, and explain choices to other people.

cold_call.foundation: Point to the next step or a feature you chose.
cold_call.middle: What did you keep or change, and why?
cold_call.higher: How does this choice support your intended effect, and what still needs checking?

ta_focus.I do: Point to the demonstrated step. Check understanding without choosing the pupil meaning.
ta_focus.We do: Ask for a pupil choice, allow thinking time and use the least help needed.
ta_focus.Independent: Support access, retain actual work or a precise witness note, and confirm the pupil words and support used.

lessons.evidence: Keep actual tests or versions, the pupil choice and reason, dated arts-log entry and actual support. A precise confirmed witness note is valid for performance or directed work. Do not prefill model answers as pupil evidence.

cover.catch_up: If prior work is missing, offer a brief honest restart: choose an invented idea and a small achievable form, state a first step and needed tools or no-materials route, then make a first version. Date it today and label it a new start. Do not claim missing earlier evidence.
cover.fallback: Use the materials-free route in each stage. For BUILD it is silent texture translation, not rubbing; for GROW use or direct the planned silent sequence. Record the actual method.
cover.stop_rule: Stop tools or sound on the agreed raised hand. Offer the quiet space and return cue. Follow the setting procedures for distress or a disclosure; do not invite public details.

lessons.title: A piece with my new texture
lessons.goal: I can use my new texture in a small piece.
success: I can use the new way I tried.
I can keep or change one part for a reason.
I can show what I did in my arts log.
words: How a surface feels or looks.
Move a tool back and forth.
With a small amount of force.
A small try before a piece.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find the tests you made last time.
Point to the one you chose.
Today you can use it in a small piece.
stages.say: Retrieve the real tests and confirmed reason. If absent or missing, make two tiny tests now with adult help; record them as today rather than inventing earlier work. Offer the same silent movement route.
stages.good: Pupil reconnects with a real choice or makes an honest new start.
stages.fallback: Recall or repeat the witnessed smooth and stop-start motions. Pupil confirms the choice.
stages.answer: A new start is valid. Do not claim an earlier trial without evidence.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Which texture did you choose?
What could it show in your piece?
You may keep your idea or change it.
stages.say: Compare the two tests. Ask the pupil to name or show one feature and a reason. A change of idea is allowed and goes in the log.
stages.good: Pupil links a visible or movement feature to an intended feeling.
stages.fallback: Pupil chooses a silent movement texture and an invented feeling.
stages.answer: The maker chooses meaning. Busy marks can feel joyful, tense or something else.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch a small texture piece.
Put paper over the safe card.
Rub lightly in two small spaces.
Leave a gap. Check your idea.
stages.say: My invented idea is energy settling down. On one small sheet I rub a ridged patch on the left and a lighter patch on the right, leaving a gap. I keep the same crayon so I can see texture and pressure. I look back at my tests. I keep the left patch and lighten the right because I want less busy marks at the end. I use the side of the crayon, with fingers outside the rubbing area. This is one adult idea, not a design to copy.
stages.good: Adult shows the technique, a deliberate choice and a small change; the pupil can make a different arrangement.
stages.fallback: Show stop-start movement, hold still for two counts, then a smooth glide and hold. Explain the shift in texture. Use a comfortable range or direct the adult.
stages.answer: CfU: How is this made: drawing each ridge, or rubbing over card under the paper? Rubbing over card. Re-show if needed.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Choose one texture for the class piece.
Where will it go?
Try one small change.
Keep or change it for a reason.
stages.say: Let pupils direct the class trial. Change the pressure or space, not every feature at once. Hinge: an adult likes a different layout. A: the pupil must copy it; B: the pupil can keep their own choice and explain.
stages.good: Pupil retains ownership and selects B.
stages.fallback: Pupil directs a smaller movement or a longer still pause and chooses its effect.
stages.answer: B. If A, model listening to advice then choosing. Parallel check: may two makers choose different textures for calm? Yes.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Make a small piece with your new texture.
Use your tests to help you choose.
Check one part. Keep it or change it.
Keep your work and your own reason.
stages.say: Use one small sheet. Place safe card beneath it and rub gently with the side of the crayon. Make two areas with a chosen space or pressure difference. A pupil may use just one texture deliberately. Stop before paper tears. Ask the pupil to choose one keep-or-change decision; do not make that decision for them. Record whether the piece is finished or still in progress.
stages.good: A small original piece shows an intentional use of rubbing and a reasoned choice, or a witnessed movement piece shows contrasting movement textures.
stages.fallback: Use or direct a short silent sequence: one texture, a still pose, a second texture, then stop. Choose the size or pace. Record the real sequence and the pupil meaning.
stages.answer: Example only: I kept the rough patch and made the next one light because I wanted the energy to fade. A one-texture piece can also be deliberate.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Show one part you chose.
Say: I kept or changed ___ because ___.
You can share with just an adult.
Tidy your space.
stages.say: Ask the maker whether the piece matches their idea. A listener notices one feature without guessing personal feelings. Use the last two minutes to collect crayons and card, remove scraps and store the work flat.
stages.good: Pupil confirms one decision and the real completion stage.
stages.fallback: Pupil repeats or directs the final movement once. Adult reads the description back for correction.
stages.answer: Keep and change are both valid when the reason relates to the intended effect.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: I tried the new way by ___.
I made ___.
I kept or changed ___ because ___.
Next I would ___.
stages.say: Retain the earlier tests with the actual piece or witness note. Record date, technique, choice, change and help. The pupil checks any scribed words. Do not claim rubbing for a movement-only response.
stages.good: The record distinguishes tests, actual piece and a next step.
stages.fallback: Use a confirmed oral entry; record at the next available opportunity.
stages.answer: Example only: I made a silent texture sequence. I changed the last move to a smooth glide to show calm.

Supported: Find or remake two small tests.
Choose a texture and direct the adult.
Make a small piece or silent sequence.
Show one choice and your reason.
Independent: Use your chosen texture in a small piece.
Check one feature against your idea.
Keep or change it for a reason.
Keep your work and dated arts-log entry.
Aspire: Compare a first version with one small change.
Explain what the change does to the feeling.
Choose the version you want to keep.

Ask the maker for their meaning and reason.

No-materials route: seated or standing silent hand movement. No device, body contact or personal story is required.

15 to 30 seconds
Rub one patch gently. Leave a gap before a second patch.
30 to 45 seconds
Make the second patch lighter. Point out the actual difference in marks.
45 to 60 seconds
Explain the decision. Show how the tests and piece stay together with a true log entry.
models: Teacher example only: the ridged marks suggest energy to me. Another maker may read them as calm.
Teacher example only: I used a smooth glide and stop-start hand movement. I chose the stops for surprise. This is movement evidence, not a rubbing.
comparison: Ridged card
Paper rests on ridges. Gentle rubbing can reveal repeated lines.
The broken lines might suggest energy.
Smoother card
Paper rests on a flatter surface. The rubbing may be more even.
The softer patch might suggest calm.

hinge.question: An adult prefers a different layout. What can the pupil do?

options.B: Keep their choice and explain why

hinge.feedback: B. Listen to the idea. The maker chooses and gives a reason.
hinge.wrong_feedback: The adult can offer a view. The maker still chooses the meaning and layout.

lessons.title: Making from my resilience plan
lessons.goal: I can start my piece from my own plan.
success: I can use my plan to start making.
I can explain a making decision.
I can record what I made and what changed.
words: Finding a way forward, with help or a change of plan.
The idea or effect you want to show.
Change part of a plan or piece.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your chosen Week 3 plan.
Say what your piece will show.
Choose a quiet way to work and share.
stages.say: Retrieve the annotated plan, tool quantities, access notes and intended effect. Pupils may use an invented seed, a path or their own abstract idea. If the plan is missing, use the brief catch-up in the cover plan. Do not claim it was made last week.
stages.good: Pupil identifies their actual plan and a first making step.
stages.fallback: Read back the retained oral sequence. If absent, the pupil chooses a simple new sequence and confirms it.
stages.answer: Resilience may involve help, rest or a different route. It does not mean ignoring discomfort.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Check your tools, space and first step.
You have 14 minutes to make today.
What small part can you make in that time?
stages.say: Check real supplies against the Week 3 plan. Its draft time split was provisional. Today the shared taught structure gives fourteen minutes of making, with a further fourteen next lesson. Scale the first section to fit; note this change in the log. Preserve the maker intention.
stages.good: Pupil sets a manageable first section and confirms actual resources.
stages.fallback: Choose a short silent sequence that can be made and repeated within fourteen minutes.
stages.answer: A smaller piece can still express the whole idea. Record a changed time or resource choice honestly.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Look back at the plan before each step.
Make a small first section.
Check the feature that shows your idea.
Record one decision as you work.
stages.say: Use an original adult plan: a line meets a block and turns towards open space. Point to the start, block and new route on the plan. On paper make the first line and block, then test the turn. My line almost touches the block, so I leave a small gap to make the new route clear. I note: I left a gap because I wanted the turn to show. For silent movement, start a forward hand path, stop, turn sideways and continue. Explain which version is actually being made.
stages.good: Adult shows plan-to-making links and a real practical decision. The adult sample is never used as pupil evidence.
stages.fallback: Model the same sequence silently with one hand. Pupil can direct position, pause or route without moving.
stages.answer: CfU: Which note records a decision: I worked hard, or I left a gap to show the turn? The second. Model a specific feature if the answer is vague.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Help check a first section against a plan.
What matches the intended idea?
Choose one small change if needed.
Say: I chose ___ because ___.
stages.say: Invite each pupil to identify one feature. Hinge: a planned material is unavailable. A: pretend it was used; B: choose an available method, keep the idea and record the change; C: copy another pupil piece.
stages.good: Pupils select B and explain how an available method can keep the intention.
stages.fallback: Offer silent movement or pupil-directed adult actions and ask which part still expresses the planned idea.
stages.answer: B. If unsure, model an unavailable paint colour replaced with pencil marks. Parallel check: a larger sheet is unavailable; can a smaller sheet work if the layout is adjusted and logged? Yes. Start making once each pupil identifies an achievable next step.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Use your Week 3 plan to make a first section.
Keep your chosen idea visible or clear in the sequence.
Pause once to check. Keep or change one feature.
Record your decision and the real next step.
stages.say: Use the pupil chosen art form. Visual route: follow the labelled layout using familiar drawing tools, paper shapes or approved paint. Sound route: use the planned short original pattern below talking volume, stop on a raised hand. Silent route: use the planned order of actions, with comfortable movement. In the fourteen minutes, use about two to set up, nine to make and three to check and note a decision; adapt to access needs. Make a first version rather than expanding the task. Staff scribe only confirmed words.
stages.good: A genuine first section or whole short first version follows the plan. The pupil records one decision, any change and the actual remaining work.
stages.fallback: Perform or direct the planned silent sequence. Adult records exact actions, order, pauses, support and confirmed intention. No media capture is needed.
stages.answer: Example only: I changed to a small sheet. I left more space round the turn to show another way forward. The final section is still to do.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Compare your work with the plan.
Ask for one useful observation.
Decide what you will keep or change next.
Store the work safely.
stages.say: A listener names a feature, then asks if it fits the maker idea. The maker can accept or decline a suggestion with a reason. Use the final two minutes for caps, water, scraps and safe storage. Keep the work with the plan; note any wet areas or loose parts.
stages.good: Pupil states what is actually made and one manageable next step.
stages.fallback: Repeat the actual sequence once, then read the witness description back for correction.
stages.answer: A useful comment is: I notice a pause before the turn. The maker decides whether that helps their intention.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: I used my plan to make ___.
I decided ___ because ___.
I changed ___ from my plan because ___.
Next lesson I need to ___.
stages.say: Record the date, actual work, decision, plan change or no change, support and next making step. If the work is incomplete, keep that clear. Preserve the pupil first version or a precise witnessed description.
stages.good: Dated record shows an actual making process rather than repeating last week planning entry.
stages.fallback: Use oral responses read back to the pupil, then retain a dated witness note.
stages.answer: A pupil may say I kept the plan because the new route was clear. Do not force a change that they do not need.

Supported: Read your plan with an adult.
Make or direct it. Pause to check.
Say one choice and what comes next.
Independent: Check your plan and available tools.
Keep or change one feature for a reason.
Log the real work, decisions and next step.
Aspire: Test two small versions of one feature.
Choose the version that fits your intention.
Keep the comparison and your reason.

log: I changed / kept ___ from my plan because ___.
The help or access method I used was ___.
My real next making step is ___.
misconceptions: Following a plan means nothing can change
Use the plan as a guide. Record a justified change in materials, layout, timing or access.
Resilience means carrying on without help
Resilience can include a pause, help or a new approach.
A plan counts as finished artwork
Keep the plan and actual making evidence distinct. State the real stage.
kit: For up to five pupils: five Week 3 plans, arts logs and actual Week 2 skill records; five pencils and small workspaces.

Check each plan materials list in advance. Drawing fallback: five sheets plus scrap and five familiar drawing tools. Paper route: clean scrap and shared glue sticks. Use familiar materials and local procedures.
For paint only if planned and approved: mats, stable water pots, brushes, a small amount of familiar washable paint and cloths. Keep wet work away from electrical equipment.
Sound needs no instrument: quiet fingertips and a stop signal. Silent movement or directed adult actions need no materials. Offer seated, quiet and private options.
Set aside five safe storage places for unfinished work with its plan and actual log. No phone or media recording is required.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Point to the adult plan: start, block, turn and open space. State the intended idea.
15 to 30 seconds
Make the first line and block or show the first two planned actions.
30 to 45 seconds
Check the turn. Leave a clearer gap or pause and say why.
45 to 60 seconds
Record the actual decision and the unfinished next step. Keep the plan with the work.
models: Teacher example only: I made the start and turn. I left a gap because it makes the new route clear. The ending still needs making.
Teacher example only: I changed a loud sound idea to silent movement. I kept the pause and turn because they show a new way forward.
comparison: Plan
A line meets a block, turns and finds open space.
Intention: another way forward.
Actual first section
The line and turn are made. The gap is wider than planned.
Decision: the wider gap makes the turn clearer. The ending is still to do.

hinge.question: A material on the plan is unavailable. What should the maker do?

options.B: Adapt the method and log the change

hinge.feedback: B. Keep the intention, use a method you have and record the real change.
hinge.wrong_feedback: Choose a method that is available. Keep the maker idea and record what changed.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Use your Week 2 skill goal while making. Compare two small versions of a feature. Ask for one useful comment. Explain which version fits your intention and why. Note a time, tool or access limit.
stretch.evidence: Keep the actual tests or witness descriptions, skill goal, feedback, pupil decision and reason.
stretch.why_optional: Your Explore work is complete without this task. Retain additional evidence for a later level review; this task does not complete a higher award.
stretch.good: Pupil applies a chosen skill, compares actual alternatives and explains a decision against intention and a real constraint.
stretch.fallback: Adult witnesses both silent versions and records the same prompts in the pupil confirmed words.

lessons.title: Developing my resilience piece
lessons.goal: I can develop my piece and explain my changes.
success: I can continue my piece from the real next step.
I can check it against my intended idea.
I can log my decisions, changes and actual stage.
words: Finding a way forward, with help or a change of plan.
The idea or effect you want to show.
Change part of a plan or piece.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your plan, first version and log.
Read the next step you chose.
Check what you can finish today.
stages.say: Reconnect the actual first version with Monday log. Let the pupil confirm or revise the next step. If absent, use the catch-up route and keep the reduced scope clear. Do not fabricate work from Monday.
stages.good: Pupil identifies existing work and a manageable continuation.
stages.fallback: Read back the actual action sequence and next step, then pupil confirms or corrects it.
stages.answer: A short piece can be enough. Record any unfinished work honestly.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Show the part that suggests resilience.
What still needs making or checking?
Choose one target for today.
stages.say: Ask the pupil to name a visible or performed feature and its intended effect. Choose one completion target within the fourteen-minute making time. It can be completing an ending, clarifying a turn or making a sequence repeatable.
stages.good: The target is specific and achievable without changing the maker intention.
stages.fallback: Select one part of the silent sequence to complete or make clearer.
stages.answer: Resilience can be shown as getting help, pausing or finding another way. Avoid personal disclosure prompts.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Look at the real first version.
Complete one planned part.
Check the effect. Try one small change.
Keep the version that fits your idea.
stages.say: Use the adult first section from Monday. Complete the new route into open space. Check whether the turn is clear. Try a longer gap on scrap or pause in the sequence; compare with the first version. I keep the short pause because it feels like a brief check before moving. I record the change from my plan and my reason. For visual work, keep the trial beside the piece; for movement, keep a precise witnessed sequence.
stages.good: Adult completes a part, compares an actual change and records the maker decision. A changed choice is not automatically an improvement.
stages.fallback: Perform the original short pause and a longer pause in the same hand sequence. Choose one and explain its effect.
stages.answer: CfU: Does a longer pause always improve the piece? No. It depends on the intended effect. Ask which version fits the maker idea.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Compare the first version with a small change.
What effect does the change have?
The maker chooses what to keep.
Say what is really finished.
stages.say: Compare the two adult versions. Hinge: only the start of a piece is made. A: record finished; B: record what exists and the next step. Ask every pupil to choose, with private pointing allowed.
stages.good: Pupil selects B and gives an accurate completion statement.
stages.fallback: Use two live silent versions and identify exactly which parts were performed.
stages.answer: B. If A, show the incomplete ending and model an honest record. Parallel check: a witness saw only the first two actions; may the record claim all four? No. Proceed when each pupil can state an actual next action.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Use your next step to develop the piece.
Keep the idea clear in the work.
Check one feature. Keep it or change it for a reason.
Keep the actual work and decisions.
stages.say: Use about two minutes to retrieve and set up, nine to complete or develop the target, and three to check and record. Adapt to access needs. The pupil can use visual art, original quiet sound or silent movement as planned. Stop sound on a raised hand. Keep wet work stable. Avoid a wholesale restart unless the pupil can explain why and accept a smaller result. If the piece is already complete, use the time to refine one feature or rehearse a repeatable sequence, recording the real decision.
stages.good: Pupil develops an actual piece and explains at least one decision, including a justified decision to keep a feature. The true completion stage is recorded.
stages.fallback: Develop or direct a short silent sequence. Staff witness the final order, pauses, changes, help and pupil meaning. No recorded media is required.
stages.answer: Example only: I completed the turn and ending. I tried a longer pause but kept the short pause because the route still feels steady.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Show a chosen part privately or to a partner.
Ask: What do you notice?
Check it against your intended idea.
Tidy and store the piece with your plan.
stages.say: Invite a respectful observation rather than praise alone. The maker states whether the observed feature matches the intention. They may keep the piece without further change. In the final two minutes tidy materials and store work safely; keep trials and logs.
stages.good: Pupil links actual features to intention, and stores evidence without claiming a later share or encounter.
stages.fallback: Adult repeats the final sequence and reads back the witness description for correction.
stages.answer: The audience can read the piece differently. The maker explanation and actual features are both worth keeping.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: My piece shows ___ through ___.
I kept or changed ___ because ___.
My piece is finished / still needs ___.
Next I would ___.
stages.say: Retain dated actual work or the final witnessed sequence, plan, decision and changes. Record support. Pupils can draw, dictate or confirm by gesture. Keep optional stretch distinct from core Explore evidence. This is making and review, not a claim that the full award is complete.
stages.good: The entry states the final current form, features, decisions, real completion stage and next step.
stages.fallback: Confirm an oral entry and record the exact witnessed version and pupil words at the next opportunity.
stages.answer: Example only: My silent piece shows another way forward through a pause and turn. It is complete as a short sequence; I would practise the ending next.

Supported: Read your next step with an adult.
Make or direct one small part.
Choose what to keep or change.
Confirm what is finished and what comes next.
Independent: Continue from the real first version.
Check one feature against your intention.
Log the actual stage and next step.
Aspire: Compare the first version and a new test.
Explain which effect fits the intention.
Use or decline feedback with a reason.

log: Today I actually made or refined ___.
My work or witness note is ___.
The piece is finished / still needs ___.
misconceptions: Following a plan means nothing can change
Use the plan as a guide. Record a justified change in materials, layout, timing or access.
Resilience means carrying on without help
Resilience can include a pause, help or a new approach.
A plan counts as finished artwork
Keep the plan and actual making evidence distinct. State the real stage.
kit: For up to five pupils: five real first versions with their Week 3 plans and Monday logs, five pencils and small workspaces. Retrieve the optional Week 2 skill records if using stretch.

Check each plan materials list in advance. Drawing fallback: five sheets plus scrap and five familiar drawing tools. Paper route: clean scrap and shared glue sticks. Use familiar materials and local procedures.
For paint only if planned and approved: mats, stable water pots, brushes, a small amount of familiar washable paint and cloths. Keep wet work away from electrical equipment.
Sound needs no instrument: quiet fingertips and a stop signal. Silent movement or directed adult actions need no materials. Offer seated, quiet and private options.
Set aside five safe storage places for unfinished work with its plan and actual log. No phone or media recording is required.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show Monday first version beside the plan and read the real next step.
15 to 30 seconds
Complete the next section or final actions.
30 to 45 seconds
Try one small change in the gap or pause. Compare both real versions.
45 to 60 seconds
Choose a version, explain why and record whether the actual piece is complete.
models: Teacher example only: I finished the route. I tested a longer gap but kept the short gap because I wanted a clear, steady turn.
Teacher example only: my final movement is forward, stop, turn, continue. I kept a short pause and can repeat the sequence.
comparison: First version
A line reaches a block and starts a turn.
The ending has not been made.
Chosen version
The new route continues into open space. A pause or gap stays short.
The maker chose a short pause after comparing both versions.

hinge.question: Only the start is made. What should the log say?

options.B: What is made and what comes next

hinge.feedback: B. Keep an honest record of actual work and the next step.
hinge.wrong_feedback: Look at the work that exists. State its real stage and the next step.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Compare your first and current versions against the Week 2 skill goal and Week 3 intention. Explain one feedback decision. Say what the tests show and what they do not show. Set a specific next practice step.
stretch.evidence: Keep actual versions or witness notes, pupil evaluation, feedback decision with reason and next skill goal.
stretch.why_optional: Your Explore work is complete without this task. Extra evidence can inform a later level review; it does not certify a higher award.
stretch.good: Pupil evaluates actual change against intention and skill, acknowledges a limit and justifies a next step.
stretch.fallback: Adult records the same evaluation prompts after witnessing the actual silent versions, using the pupil confirmed words.
